data.title: The numbers: Asian Games
data.description: Asian Games achievements underlined over the numbers.
data.spot: Athletics Podium summarised the hidden numbers of this memorable Asian Games edition in Aichi prefecture, Japan.

image.caption: Triple gold medallist Winfred Yavi and her bitter rival, Nozomi Tanaka of Japan.

data.content:
The most important athletics meet on the most populous continent was over. In Aichi-Nagoya, the six-day, highly entertaining contest satisfied the athletics fans. Among the many historic achievements, two young sprinters came a step ahead: Thai speed king Puripol Boonson and Yujie Chen, the 17-year-old Chinese prodigy.

As Boonson equalled the 200 metres Asian record in a fascinating final on a rainy day, Chinese hammer thrower Jiale Zhang crushed the continental record with her monstrous 78.27 metres effort. Equally magical, yet another 17-year-old phenomenon, Yan Ziyi, avenged Olympic champion Haruka Kitaguchi from the Ultimate Championships in Budapest with a single throw that landed in a massive length: 70.46 metres.


NATION SHORTNOTES

CHN: Same number of medals as 2023, but fewer golds. (32)

JPN: Most titles since 1998. (10)

BRN: Fourth straight games with 9+ titles; however, the fewest total (13).

THA: Best achievement since 1978. Only the third time 3+ titles.

UZB: Second time took 3 golds (First in their debut in 1994).

IND: 24 total medals but a single gold. Least titles since 2006.

IRI: Six straight Games with a title. 4 total medals. (Most 8 in Tehran 1974)

QAT: Least successful Games since 2002, but their gold streak hits 11 Games (since 1986)
